les: Sewe gelowe, en waaraan jy elkeen ken - deel 2
kaps_punt: Kennis van die meerderheidsgelowe in Suid-Afrika (deel 2 van 2): Boeddhisme, Baha'i-geloof, Afrika-religie: Betekenisvolle plekke, geboue en aanbiddingsimbole van verskillende religieë.

items.bewering: Afrika-religie is 'n lewende geloof wat baie mense in Suid-Afrika vandag beoefen.
items.bron: SA History Online, 'African traditional religion' (https://www.sahistory.org.za/article/african-traditional-religion): calls it 'very popular' and says it is often combined with Christianity and Islam; GCIS pocket guide 'South Africa's People' (https://www.gcis.gov.za/sites/default/files/docs/resourcecentre/pocketguide/2009/004_sa_people.pdf); General Household Survey 2013 summary (~5% identify with ancestral/traditional African religion, i.e. millions of people, before counting those who combine it with Christianity) via https://businesstech.co.za/news/lifestyle/126445/the-most-popular-religions-in-south-africa/.

items.bewering: Die plekke wat vir hierdie geloof saak maak, is dikwels nie geboue nie. Die huis self is een daarvan en by baie mense ook die beeskraal.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Kraal' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kraal): the Zulu cattle enclosure (isibaya) is 'an important site for communicating with ancestor spirits', and each hut holds an umsamo, a special ritual area; a scholarly paper on Southern Bantu religion (search result, UKZN Alternation, https://alternation.ukzn.ac.za/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/13-Ngobese-min.pdf) places ancestors at the back of the main hut and at the cattle kraal. True as written. One wording note, not a fact fault: the first place given (the house) is itself a building, straight after 'dikwels nie geboue nie'. What is true is that ATR has no special building for worship like a church or temple. The writer may want to sharpen this, but it is not false.

items.bewering: Die grafte van die voorouers is vir baie gesinne heilig.
items.bron: GCIS pocket guide 'South Africa's People' (ancestors of far greater importance than the Supreme Being; kept in good standing with ritual offerings); Mail & Guardian, 'Cows: the sacred and the profane' (https://mg.co.za/friday/2016-04-07-cows-the-sacred-and-the-profane/), on funerary and ancestral rituals; UP monograph on sacred sites (https://upmonographs.up.ac.za/index.php/ESI/catalog/download/7/43/108?inline=1).

items.bewering: Party plekke in die veld word ook heilig gehou en nie sommer besoek nie.
items.bron: University of Pretoria monograph (https://upmonographs.up.ac.za/index.php/ESI/catalog/download/7/43/108?inline=1): names Phiphidi Falls (Vhavenda) and other natural sacred sites; UKZN Alternation paper on sacred caves in the eastern Free State; scholarship on Nguni sacred mountains.

items.bewering: Afrika-religie is nie een godsdiens met een gebou en een teken nie. Van plek tot plek en van volk tot volk lyk die gebruike anders.
items.bron: SAHO ATR article ties practices to specific peoples (Zulu, Xhosa, Nguni); research on ancestors (e.g. https://www.ajol.info/index.php/ijcrh/article/view/259722) notes that criteria and practices 'vary according to different societies'; a UCT Press volume on traditional religion in SA law (https://openuctpress.uct.ac.za/uctpress/catalog/download/28/34/124?inline=1) stresses how hard it is to define as one category.

items.bewering: Die respek vir die voorouers is die draad wat deur die meeste van hierdie gebruike loop.
items.bron: 'die meeste' is a majority quantifier, so it is checked as a superlative. GCIS pocket guide: ancestors 'of far greater importance', appeased by regular ritual offerings; SAHO: 'ancestors are part of every major event'; Hammond-Tooke (cited in the UKZN paper): the ancestral spirit is the foundation of Southern Bantu religion. Sources support 'most'.

items.bewering: By baie mense brand daar impepho om die voorouers nader te roep.
items.bron: Zondi & Ntshangase, Alternation (UKZN) (https://alternation.ukzn.ac.za/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/12-Zon-min.pdf): the dried herb is burned to communicate with ancestors; International Society for Ethnopharmacology photo essay (https://ethnopharmacology.org/helichrysum-a-ritual-plant-and-its-therapeutic-potential-a-photo-essay/): burned by Zulu, Xhosa and Ndebele people to invoke ancestors, and a healer says the smoke brings ancestors close; Wikipedia 'Helichrysum petiolare'.

items.bewering: Baie mense dra kraalwerk as deel van hulle kultuur se klere. Jy sien dit in die hare en om die polse en die nek.
items.bron: V&A collections, Xhosa/Zulu beadwork necklaces (https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O350/necklace-unknown): beadwork shows the wearer's ethnicity, age, region and status, and Xhosa and Zulu women still make and wear a lot of it; Harvard Peabody beadwork records; Zulu beaded headdresses (https://valeriehector.com/blog/zulu-beaded-sangoma-wigs).

items.bewering: By 'n tradisionele geneser soos 'n sangoma is die krale wel 'n teken van geloof. Dit geld ook vir iemand wat leer om so 'n geneser te word.
items.bron: Sowetan, 'Five facts casting light on ubungoma' (https://www.sowetan.co.za/good-life/2021-03-01-five-facts-casting-light-on-ubungoma/): red and white neck beads stand for helping spirits and mark izangoma; fully trained initiates wear izangoma bracelets and anklets. Wikipedia 'Ukuthwasa' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukuthwasa): a Gauteng learner in initiation wore 'sangoma beads' (iintsimbi) at school, so trainees wear them too.

items.bewering: Krale alleen wys jou dus nie wat iemand glo nie.
items.bron: Follows from the two sources above. The V&A treats beadwork as cultural identity and courtship communication ('love letters'), not as a religious marker, while sangoma beads are religious. Wearing beads alone does not show belief.

items.bewering: Baie mense in Suid-Afrika beoefen Afrika-religie en die Christendom saam.
items.bron: GCIS pocket guide 'South Africa's People' (https://www.gcis.gov.za/sites/default/files/docs/resourcecentre/pocketguide/2003/people.pdf): many people find themselves between traditional African religion and Christianity; SAHO: ATR is 'often combined with elements of Christianity'; In die Skriflig 38(1), 2004 (https://www.doi.org/10.4102/ids.v38i1.419) and other SA theological studies document ancestor veneration among African Christians.

items.bewering: Baie Boeddhiste gaan na 'n tempel toe om daar te aanbid.
items.bron: Nan Hua Temple's own site (https://www.nanhuatemple.org/history): main temple, shrine halls and weekly visitors; Sri Lankan Ministry of Foreign Affairs (https://mfa.gov.lk/?p=58644): Vesak observed at the Thai temple in Midrand. 'Aanbid' fits, given the lesson's own definition ('wat vir hulle heilig is').

items.bewering: Die Nan Hua-tempel by Bronkhorstspruit in Gauteng is so 'n plek.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Nan Hua Temple' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nan_Hua_Temple): in the Cultura Park suburb of Bronkhorstspruit; Wikipedia 'Bronkhorstspruit' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bronkhorstspruit): a town in Gauteng, run by the City of Tshwane since 2011; nanhuatemple.org.

items.bewering: Die dakke van die geboue krul aan die punte op soos Chinese dakke.
items.bron: nanhuatemple.org/history: built in Chinese style, with glazed clay roof tiles from Taiwan; fabriziomusacchio.com (2025): 'traditional Chinese architectural style, with prayer halls, pagodas'; China Highlights (https://www.chinahighlights.com/travelguide/architecture/roofs.htm) and an MDPI Buildings study (https://www.mdpi.com/2075-5309/15/14/2582): upturned eaves are the signature of Chinese temple roofs. No source describes Nan Hua's eaves in words, so this rests on its stated traditional Chinese style. The comparison holds, because the roofs are built in that tradition.

items.bewering: Besoekers stap deur die tuine en tussen die geboue van die tempel rond.
items.bron: nanhuatemple.org: open to visitors, free Sunday temple tours; Bronkhorstspruit trip and tourism listings (wanderlog, airial.travel) describe 'meticulously maintained gardens'; the complex covers over 2.4 km² (Wikipedia).

items.bewering: Ander Boeddhistiese tempels staan ook in dorpe en stede regoor die land.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Nan Hua Temple': it 'has opened branches in other South African cities', in Johannesburg, Bloemfontein, Newcastle, Durban and Cape Town; Thai Buddhist temple, Midrand (mfa.gov.lk); Kadampa urban temple, Durban, opened March 2023 (https://kadampa.org/2023/03/grand-opening-ceremony-of-kmc-durban).

items.bewering: In 'n Boeddhistiese tempel staan of sit daar gewoonlik 'n beeld van die Boeddha. Die beeld sit dikwels met die bene gekruis en die rug regop.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Iconography of Gautama Buddha in Laos and Thailand' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iconography_of_Gautama_Buddha_in_Laos_and_Thailand): seated cross-legged lotus posture; Toledo Museum of Art, 'Seated Buddha' (https://emuseum.toledomuseum.org/objects/56199/seated-buddha); Carleton 'Buddha Statues' exhibit (https://religionsmn.carleton.edu/exhibits/show/wattmunisotaram/the-watt-munisotaram---campus/statues-and-symbolism).

items.bewering: Op baie beelde is die gesig kalm en die oë halfpad toe.
items.bron: Brooklyn Museum guide (https://cms-files.brooklynmuseum.org/eb82346f075748e59d7158c094039c74bab70d54.pdf): half-closed eyes signal meditation and inner calm; Japan MLIT multilingual temple text on a seated Amida Buddha (https://www.mlit.go.jp/tagengo-db/common/001565162.pdf); Ashmolean Jameel Centre (serenity). 'Op baie' is correctly hedged.

items.bewering: Op Boeddhistiese tempels en boeke sien jy ook 'n wiel met speke. Daardie wiel is 'n teken by baie plekke waar Boeddhiste bymekaarkom.
items.bron: Metropolitan Museum, 'Wheel of the Buddhist Law (Rinpō)' (https://www.metmuseum.org/art/collection/search/53183): the dharmachakra symbolises the Buddha's teaching, with eight spokes; ReligionFacts 'Dharma wheel' (https://religionfacts.com/dharma-wheel): spokes usually eight.

items.bewering: Die gebou van die Baha'i-geloof word 'n huis van aanbidding genoem.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Baháʼí House of Worship' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bah%C3%A1%CA%BC%C3%AD_House_of_Worship); Bahá'í World News Service (https://news.bahai.org/story/806).

items.bewering: So 'n gebou het nege sye en nege deure na buite.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Baháʼí House of Worship': 'a nine-sided design', and 'nine doors' is among the features 'Abdu'l-Bahá specified; the Lotus Temple's petals form nine entryways; Bahai Library Online, Iranica 'Bahai temples' (https://www.bahai-library.com/rafati_iranica_bahai_temples): a nine-sided circular shape is essential; Wilmette is described with nine sides and nine doors.

items.bewering: Die deure gaan van alle kante oop sodat mense van enige geloof kan inkom.
items.bron: Bahá'í World News Service, 'Golden anniversary for temple of light' (https://news.bahai.org/story/218/): nine doors 'open to every direction', a symbol of unity because it is open to everyone to pray there; Wikipedia: Houses of Worship are 'open to all people regardless of religion'. The stated reason matches the faith's own account.

items.bewering: 'n Ronde dak sit gewoonlik bo-op die gebou, en jy kan dit van ver af sien.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Baháʼí House of Worship': Shoghi Effendi's guidance that 'all Baháʼí temples should have a dome'; University of Idaho architecture page (https://www.webpages.uidaho.edu/arch499/nonwest/bahai/house.htm): all current Houses of Worship have a dome; Kampala dome over 37 m high (Wikipedia 'Kampala Baháʼí Temple'). 'Gewoonlik' correctly covers unusual forms such as the Lotus Temple.

items.bewering: Daar is nie baie sulke geboue in die hele wêreld nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Baháʼí House of Worship' listings: about 14 standing worldwide (8 continental, 2 national, 4 local); the Ashgabat one was destroyed. 'Not many' is accurate.

items.bewering: Die eerste een in Afrika staan in Kampala in Uganda.
items.bron: Bahá'í World News Service, 'Fifty years on, Uganda's Baha'i temple...' (https://news.bahai.org/story/806): 'The first Bahá'í House of Worship on the continent — known as the "Mother Temple of Africa"', built on Kikaya Hill outside Kampala, dedicated January 1961; Wikipedia 'Kampala Baháʼí Temple' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kampala_Bah%C3%A1%CA%BC%C3%AD_Temple): the world's third House of Worship. The later African ones (Kenya local, DRC national) date from the 2020s. 'Die eerste' holds, and 'staan' is right: the building is still standing.

items.bewering: Baha'i-gemeenskappe in Suid-Afrika kom in hulle eie sentrums en in mekaar se huise bymekaar.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Baháʼí Faith in South Africa' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bah%C3%A1%CA%BC%C3%AD_Faith_in_South_Africa): a Baháʼí Faith Centre in Mdantsane, beginnings in a private home in Sea Point (1911), and no House of Worship in SA mentioned; bahai.org 'Devotional meetings' (https://www.bahai.org/sw/action/devotional-life/devotional-meetings): informal gatherings, largely in homes; Bahá'í Journal UK 2004 (https://bahai-library.com/bjuk/bjuk_2004_jan-feb_v20_n5_9_South_Africa.pdf): a weekly devotional meeting in East London. Read with the block above, the lesson rightly implies that SA Baha'is meet without a House of Worship.

items.bewering: 'n Ster met nege punte is die teken wat 'n mens die meeste by hierdie geloof sien. Jy sien die negepuntige ster op geboue, op boeke en op kettings.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Baháʼí symbols' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bah%C3%A1%CA%BC%C3%AD_symbols): number 9 symbols are used often, and 'the most common of these is the nine-pointed star'; Bahaipedia 'Nine-pointed star' (https://bahaipedia.org/Nine-pointed_star). Caution, which the lesson already respects: Shoghi Effendi named the five-pointed star (haykal) as the Faith's symbol and said the nine-pointed star is not part of the teachings. The lesson claims only what is seen most, which is true. It must not be reworded to call it the official or holy symbol of the faith.

items.bewering: In 'n huis van aanbidding staan daar geen beelde of prente nie.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Baháʼí House of Worship': Baháʼí law says 'no pictures, statues, or images may be displayed within Houses of Worship'; University of Idaho page: not decorated with statues or pictures inside.

items.bewering: Al sewe hierdie gelowe word in Suid-Afrika langs mekaar beoefen.
items.bron: GCIS pocket guide 'South Africa's People' (religious affiliation tables: Christianity, Islam, Hinduism, Judaism, traditional African religion and others); Wikipedia 'Buddhism in South Africa' (about 0.2–0.3%, roughly 100 000–150 000 people); Wikipedia 'Baháʼí Faith in South Africa' (since 1911, National Spiritual Assembly 1995). This lesson names only three of the seven by name, plus church, mosque and Hindu temple. Every faith it implies is present in SA.

items.bewering: In een dorp kan 'n kerk, 'n moskee en 'n tempel naby mekaar staan.
items.bron: Framed as a possibility ('kan'). Durban: the Somtseu Road Hindu temple (1875, https://sanationalsociety.co.za/somtseu-road-hindu-temple/), Buddhist temples (Kadampa, Nan Hua branch) and many churches and mosques share one city.

items.bewering: By party plekke trek besoekers hulle skoene uit voordat hulle ingaan.
items.bron: Tanenbaum Center, 'Entering Sacred Spaces: Visiting Religious Homes' (https://tanenbaum.org/about-us/tanenbaum-resources/visiting-religious-homes/); Hindu Endowments Board Singapore temple etiquette (https://heb.org.sg/temple-etiquette/); adventure-life Buddhist/Hindu temple etiquette. Shoes come off at mosques, Hindu temples and Buddhist shrine halls. 'Party plekke' is accurate.

items.bewering: voorouers: Die mense in jou familie van wie jy afstam en wat reeds oorlede is, soos 'n ouma of oupa wat al gesterf het.
items.bron: Scholarly accounts of ATR ancestors (https://www.ajol.info/index.php/ijcrh/article/view/259722; https://jamesbishopblog.com/2022/03/04/what-are-the-ancestors-in-african-traditional-religion/): deceased family members who stay present ('living-dead'); GCIS: 'the deceased elders of the group'. Simplified correctly for Grade 4. Strictly, some traditions do not count every dead relative as an ancestor (criteria differ by society), but the definition does not claim that every relative is one.

items.bewering: beeskraal: Die plek binne 'n heining waar 'n familie se beeste snags aangehou word.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Kraal': an enclosure for cattle, usually fenced with thornbush, palisade or mud wall; Dictionary of South African English, 'kraal' (verb) (https://dsae.co.za/entry/kraal/e04090): cattle penned each evening; Kolb's account of Khoikhoi herds brought in from pasture in the evening.

items.bewering: impepho: 'n Geurige plant wat mense brand om hul voorouers nader te roep en met hulle te praat.
items.bron: Helichrysum species (Wikipedia 'Helichrysum petiolare', https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helichrysum_petiolare, which notes the aromatic foliage); Zondi & Ntshangase (UKZN Alternation): burned to communicate with ancestors; ISE photo essay. The glossary entry also reads correctly on its own.

items.bewering: kraalwerk: Klein gekleurde krale wat in patrone aanmekaargewerk word.
items.bron: V&A collections (Xhosa/Zulu beadwork: bead embroidery whose colour and design carry meaning); Metropolitan Museum record on southern African beadwork (https://www.metmuseum.org/ru/art/collection/search/314789): glass beads imported from the late 18th century.

items.bewering: sangoma: 'n Tradisionele geneser wat met die voorouers werk om mense te help.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Traditional healers of Southern Africa' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_healers_of_Southern_Africa); Wikipedia 'Ukuthwasa' (sangomas are called by and work with ancestors); Sowetan 'Five facts casting light on ubungoma'.

items.bewering: tempel: 'n Gebou waar Hindoes, Boeddhiste en mense van party ander gelowe aanbid.
items.bron: Pluralism Project 'Temple' (https://pluralism.org/temple) and Wikipedia 'Temple' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple): Hindu, Buddhist and Jain temples, among others. 'Party ander gelowe' is correctly open-ended. It fits the lesson's choice to call the Baha'i building a 'huis van aanbidding' rather than a tempel.

items.bewering: aanbidding: Om God, of wat vir hulle heilig is, te eer en respek te wys, soos deur te bid, te sing of te buig.
items.bron: Wiktionary 'aanbid' (https://en.wiktionary.com/wiki/aanbid): worship, religious veneration; NGTT article (https://ojs.reformedjournals.co.za/index.php/ngtt/article/download/807/1208/1639) on aanbidding as religious veneration. The phrase 'of wat vir hulle heilig is' correctly covers Buddhists and ancestor veneration, where 'God' alone would not fit.

items.bewering: negepuntige ster: 'n Ster met nege punte wat 'n mens die meeste by die Baha'i-geloof sien.
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Baháʼí symbols': the nine-pointed star is the most common nine-symbol. The entry also reads correctly on its own, because it claims frequency, not official status. Same caution as the study-block item: do not tighten it to 'die simbool van die geloof', since the official symbol is the five-pointed star.

items.bewering: Read as a set, the parallel blocks (Afrika-religie: places and signs; Boeddhisme: temple and signs; Baha'i: building and signs; 'Sewe gelowe in een land') imply no false contrast or ranking between the faiths.
items.blok: Afrika-religie se plekke; Waaraan jy Afrika-religie ken; Die Boeddhistiese tempel; Waaraan jy Boeddhisme ken; Die Baha'i-huis van aanbidding; Waaraan jy die Baha'i-geloof ken; Sewe gelowe in een land
items.bron: Contrasts checked across the set, each against the sources above. (1) Buddha image in the temple vs no images in a Baha'i House of Worship: a real contrast, sourced (Baháʼí law; Buddhist iconography). (2) ATR 'nie een godsdiens met een gebou en een teken nie', set beside faiths each given a building and a sign. The other blocks are hedged ('gewoonlik', 'baie', 'dikwels', 'die meeste'), and Buddhism is given two signs, so they do not claim the other faiths are uniform. That ATR has no central institution or single worship building is well sourced (SAHO, GCIS, UCT Press). (3) Baha'i: the lesson describes a building SA does not have, but immediately says SA communities meet in centres and homes, so no false presence is implied. (4) Ranking: no faith is called older, larger, truer or more widespread than another. The only quantities are hedged frequency words inside one faith, and the closing block treats all seven as equal neighbours. (5) The lists of signs within each faith are not set against each other as if exhaustive.

opsomming: All 39 items are confirmed: 38 claims plus the set check of the parallel faith blocks, which implies no false contrast or ranking. The four superlatives hold, including the Kampala temple as the first in Africa and the nine-pointed star as the Baha'i sign seen most often, which stays true only as long as no revision calls it the official symbol, because that is the five-pointed star. One optional wording note: 'often not buildings' is followed by the house as the first example.
